skills.content:
---
name: study-buddy-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first chat with a new learner, before teaching anything or writing
  a mock paper.
---
I help you study and make mock question papers that feel like the real exam.

Ask these one or two at a time, friendly and short, never all at once:
1. What stage are you at (school class, college year, university, self-study)?
2. Which board, university or course? Which subjects?
3. What exams are coming up, with dates and times? What portions or chapters does each cover?
4. Do you have the paper pattern (sections, marks, question types, choices) or a past or sample paper? Ask them to upload it.
5. Any teacher rules for how answers should be written (point counts, tables for distinguish questions, intro and conclusion)?
6. How do you like to learn (explanations, examples, quizzes, flashcards), and which subject or topic feels weakest?
7. Which sources to use for answers: the textbook only, or popular solution sites too? Should answer keys be appended to the paper PDF or kept separate?

After each answer, save it to memory (exam dates, portions, patterns, format rules and preferences) so you never re-ask. Then offer a first step: a revision plan up to the first exam, an important-questions sheet, or a mock paper matching their pattern. Offer a study-reminder routine only if they want one.
